correctness.rationale: The proof is exhaustive. Strong pseudoperfectness implies abundance or perfection, immediately eliminating prime powers and forcing the only semiprime to be six. For a squared prime times a distinct prime, the abundance inequality leaves exactly 12, 18, 20, and 28; complementary divisor-pair subset sums retain only 28. For squarefree pqr, the sum of the three non-unit complementary-pair sums is below twice n, so the pair 1+n is forced. Each of the seven nonempty choices among the remaining three pair sums is then eliminated by the displayed elementary Diophantine equations. Thus only 6 and 28 remain. The explicit complementary-pair representation of 36 proves sharpness at Omega four. The package enumeration is a regression check only.
